descriptions.en: Sit on a bench with the back supported and hold a dumbbell at each shoulder, palms facing you. Press upward while gradually rotating the palms forward. Reverse the rotation while lowering under control. Keep the trunk still and avoid forcing the shoulders through an uncomfortable range. Record the weight of one dumbbell.

Position barbell overhead with narrow overhand grip.
Lower forearm behind upper arm with elbows remaining overhead. Extend forearm overhead. Lower and repeat.
descriptions.it:
Posizionare il bilanciere in alto con una presa stretta.
Abbassare l'avambraccio dietro il braccio superiore mantenendo i gomiti in alto. Estendere l'avambraccio sopra la testa. Abbassare e ripetere.

descriptions.en: Set a flat bench inside a rack and position the supports and safeties. Lie with the feet planted and shoulder blades supported. Hold the bar slightly wider than shoulder width, unrack it, and lower toward the chest under control. Press upward without bouncing or lifting the hips. Return the bar securely to the rack. Record the total barbell weight.
descriptions.it: Distensione Panca Piana con BilanciereDistensione Panca Piana con Bilanciere

descriptions.en:
• 
Setup and Starting Position: Sit at the end of a flat bench with a dumbbell resting vertically against each thigh. Carefully lean back while driving the dumbbells toward your chest with your knees.

• 
The “Leg Drive” and Posture: Plant your feet firmly on the floor. Retract your shoulder blades (press them together against the bench) and maintain a slight natural lumbar curve.

• 
Starting Position: Push the dumbbells toward the ceiling. Your wrists should be aligned with your elbows. Rotate the dumbbells slightly inward (about 45 degrees) so that your elbows do not splay out too far to the sides, thereby protecting your shoulders.

• 
Eccentric Phase (Lowering): Lower the dumbbells in a controlled manner toward the sides of your chest. Your elbows should lower at an angle of about 45–60 degrees relative to your body. Feel the stretch in the lower part of your chest.

• 
Concentric Phase (Lift): Push the weight upward in a slight arc (toward the center), without letting the dumbbells collide at the top or fully locking out your elbows to maintain muscle tension. Exhale as you lift.

Translated with DeepL.com (free version)
descriptions.it:
Il movimento è molto simile a quello della panca con bilanciere, ma il peso viene portato al petto in un punto più basso.
Impugnate due manubri e sdraiatevi su una panca. Tenete i pesi vicino al petto, all'altezza dei capezzoli, e spingeteli verso l'alto fino a tendere le braccia. Lasciare scendere il peso lentamente e in modo controllato.

descriptions.en: Set a flat bench inside a rack with the supports and safeties positioned. Lie with the feet planted and hold the bar around shoulder width. Unrack it and lower toward the lower chest with the elbows near the torso. Press upward under control without bouncing, then return the bar securely to the rack. Record the total barbell weight.
descriptions.it: Sdraiatevi su una panca, il bilanciere è direttamente sopra gli occhi, le ginocchia formano un leggero angolo e i piedi sono ben saldi a terra. Impugnare la sbarra con una presa stretta (circa 20 cm). Portare il peso lentamente verso il basso fino a quando le braccia sono parallele al pavimento (gomito: angolo retto), premere poi il bilanciere verso l'alto. Quando si porta il bilanciere verso il basso, non farlo scendere sui capezzoli come nel normale esercizio di panca, ma un po' più in basso.

descriptions.en: Place one knee and the hand on the same side on a stable bench. Keep the other foot on the floor and hold one dumbbell in the free hand. Brace the trunk and keep the back still. Pull the dumbbell toward the hip by driving the elbow backward, without rotating the torso or shrugging. Lower under control to a straight arm. Complete the prescribed repetitions on each side; record the weight of the single dumbbell.

Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand. Bend the knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping the trunk braced and the back still. With a small fixed bend in the elbows, raise the arms out to the sides without shrugging or swinging. Lower under control. No bench is required. Record the weight of one dumbbell.

• Holding a barbell with a pronated grip (palms facing down), bend your knees slightly and bring your torso forward, by bending at the waist, while keeping the back straight until it is almost parallel to the floor. Tip: Make sure that you keep the head up. The barbell should hang directly in front of you as your arms hang perpendicular to the floor and your torso. This is your starting position.
• Now, while keeping the torso stationary, breathe out and lift the barbell to you. Keep the elbows close to the body and only use the forearms to hold the weight. At the top contracted position, squeeze the back muscles and hold for a brief pause.
• Then inhale and slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
• Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
descriptions.it: Impugnando un bilanciere con presa in pronazione (palmi rivolti verso il basso), piegare leggermente le ginocchia e portare il busto in avanti, piegando in vita, mantenendo la schiena dritta fino a portarla quasi parallela al pavimento. Suggerimento: assicurati di tenere la testa alta. Il bilanciere dovrebbe pendere direttamente davanti a te mentre le tue braccia pendono perpendicolarmente al pavimento e al busto. Questa è la tua posizione di partenza.     Ora, mantenendo fermo il busto, espira e solleva il bilanciere verso di te. Tieni i gomiti vicini al corpo e usa solo gli avambracci per sostenere il peso. Nella posizione contratta in alto, contrai i muscoli della schiena e mantieni la posizione per una breve pausa.     Quindi inspira e abbassa lentamente il bilanciere nella posizione iniziale.     Ripeti per la quantità consigliata di ripetizioni.

descriptions.en: Stand holding a barbell with an underhand grip around shoulder width. Bend the knees slightly and hinge forward, keeping the trunk braced. Pull the bar toward the lower ribs with the elbows close to the torso. Lower under control until the arms are extended, keeping the torso angle constant without swinging. Record the total barbell weight.

Stand with the feet stable and hold the barbell around shoulder width. Brace the trunk, keep the shoulders down, and hold the elbows close to the sides. Curl the bar by flexing the elbows without leaning back or driving the elbows forward. Stop before the shoulders take over, then lower the bar slowly to full extension while keeping the wrists neutral.
descriptions.it: Curl con bilanciereCurl con bilanciere

descriptions.en: Stand or sit with one dumbbell in each hand, arms extended and palms initially facing inward. Keep the upper arms close to the torso and curl the dumbbells with a controlled motion, rotating the palms upward if comfortable. Pause near the top without moving the elbows forward, then lower slowly until the elbows are fully extended. Do not swing the torso.
descriptions.it:
Impugnare due manubri, le braccia sono distese, le mani sono sul fianco, i palmi rivolti verso l'interno. Piegare le braccia e portare il peso con un movimento veloce verso l'alto. Allo stesso tempo, ruotate le braccia di 90 gradi all'inizio del movimento. Nel punto più alto, ruotate un po' i pesi verso l'esterno. Senza fare pause, riportateli giù, lentamente.
Non lasciate che il corpo oscilli durante l'esercizio, tutto il lavoro è svolto dai bicipiti, che sono gli unici muscoli che devono muoversi (fate attenzione ai gomiti).

descriptions.en: Stand upright holding the EZ bar with a comfortable angled grip. Brace the trunk and keep the elbows close to the sides. Curl the bar by bending the elbows while keeping the shoulders quiet and the wrists aligned with the forearms. Pause briefly near the top, then lower the bar under control to full extension. Avoid leaning backward or accelerating the weight.

Stand tall facing a low cable with the handle held at shoulder width. Keep the ribs down, shoulders relaxed, and elbows close to the torso. Curl the handle by bending only the elbows until the forearms approach the upper arms. Pause without letting the elbows drift forward, then lower the load under control to full elbow extension. Avoid swinging or using momentum.

• Adjust the seat height so that the grips are parallel to your chest.
• Use your legs to push the foot forward pedal.
• Bring the handles to the start position.
• Keep your back in contact with the back pad, press outwards.
• Press the handles away from your chest and exhale.
• Allow the handles to come in gently until they reach your chest.
• Allow the handles to return to your chest as you inhale.

Sit on the butterfly machine, the feet have a good contact with the floor, the upper arms are parallel to the floor. Press your arms together till the handles are practically together (but aren't!). Go slowly back. The weights should stay all the time in the air.

Adjust the reverse pec deck seat so the handles are around shoulder height. Sit facing the chest pad and hold the handles with a small bend in the elbows. Open the arms out and backward without shrugging or arching the lower back. Return slowly until the arms are in front of you. Keep the chest supported throughout. Record the selected machine load.

Put  the balls of your feet on an extended leg press pad.  Use your calves to press the weight by flexing your feet/toes into a pointed position, and releasing back into a relaxed position.
This exercise builds mass and strength in the Gastrocnemius and Soleus muscles as well, if not better, than any calf exercise.
descriptions.it:
Metter le punte dei piedi sulla base di spinta della leg press. Usate i polpacci per premere il peso flettendo i piedi/le dita dei piedi in una posizione appuntita e rilasciandoli in una posizione rilassata.
Questo esercizio aumenta la massa e la forza dei muscoli Gastrocnemio e Soleo come, se non meglio, di qualsiasi altro esercizio per i polpacci.

descriptions.en: The chin-up (also known as a chin or chinup) is a strength training exercise. People frequently do this exercise with the intention of strengthening muscles such as the latissimus dorsi and biceps, which extend the shoulder and flex the elbow, respectively. In this maneuver, the palms are faced towards the body. It is a form of pull-up in which the range of motion is established in relation to a person's chin.
descriptions.it: Il chin-up (noto anche come mento o chinup) è un esercizio di allenamento della forza. Le persone spesso eseguono questo esercizio con l'intenzione di rafforzare muscoli come il gran dorsale e il bicipite, che rispettivamente estendono la spalla e flettono il gomito. In questa manovra, i palmi sono rivolti verso il corpo. È una forma di pull-up in cui il range di movimento è stabilito in relazione al mento di una persona.

descriptions.en: Grasp a moderately weighted dumbbell so your palms are flat against the underside of the top plates and your thumbs are around the bar. Lie on your back across a flat bench so only your upper back and shoulders are in contact with the bench. Your feet should be set about shoulder-width apart and your head should hang slightly downward. With the dumbbell supported at arm's length directly about your chest, bend your arms about 15 degrees and keep them bent throughout the movement. Slowly lower the dumbbell backward and downward in a semicircle arc to as low a position as is comfortably possible. Raise it slowly back along the same arc to the starting point, and repeat for the required number of repetitions.
descriptions.it: Afferra un manubrio di peso moderato in modo che i palmi delle mani siano piatti contro la parte inferiore delle piastre superiori e i pollici siano attorno alla barra. Sdraiati sulla schiena su una panca piana in modo che solo la parte superiore della schiena e le spalle siano a contatto con la panca. I tuoi piedi dovrebbero essere posizionati alla larghezza delle spalle e la tua testa dovrebbe pendere leggermente verso il basso. Con il manubrio appoggiato a distanza di un braccio direttamente sul petto, piega le braccia di circa 15 gradi e tienile piegate per tutto il movimento. Abbassa lentamente il manubrio all'indietro e verso il basso in un arco di semicerchio nella posizione più bassa possibile. Sollevalo lentamente lungo lo stesso arco fino al punto di partenza e ripeti per il numero richiesto di ripetizioni.

descriptions.en: Lie on your back with the knees bent and feet supported. Place the fingertips lightly beside the head or cross the arms over the chest without pulling on the neck. Exhale and curl the ribs toward the pelvis until the shoulder blades lift from the floor. Keep the lower back comfortably supported, pause, and lower slowly. Use a small controlled range rather than momentum.
descriptions.it:
• Sdraiati a pancia in su sul pavimento con le ginocchia piegate.
• Solleva il busto verso il bacino, a 30° / 40° dal suolo. Le mani possono essere dietro o accanto al collo o incrociate sul petto.
• Ripeti

descriptions.en: The procedure is very similar as for regular crunches, only with the additional weight of the machine. Sit on the machine, put both feet firmly on the ground. Grab the to the weights, cables, etc. and do a rolling motion forwards (the spine should ideally lose touch vertebra by vertebra). Slowly return to the starting position.

Attach a rope to a high cable and kneel facing the stack. Hold the rope beside the temples with the elbows bent. Curl the ribs toward the pelvis by flexing the trunk, keeping the hips mostly still. Return slowly without pulling with the arms or turning the movement into a hip hinge. Record the selected cable load.

Stand firmly, with your feet slightly more than shoulder wide apart. Stand directly behind the bar where it should barely touch your shin, your feet pointing a bit out. Bend down with a straight back, the knees also pointing somewhat out. Grab the bar with a shoulder wide grip, one overhand, one underhand (mixed grip).
Pull the weight up. At the highest point make a slight hollow back and pull the bar back. Hold 1 or 2 seconds that position. Go down, making sure the back is not bent. Once down you can either go back again as soon as the weights touch the floor, or make a pause, depending on the weight.
descriptions.it:
StaccoStacco
Stacco

descriptions.en: Set a decline bench in a rack with the supports and safeties positioned. Secure the legs using the bench supports and hold the bar slightly wider than shoulder width. Unrack it, lower toward the lower chest under control, then press upward without bouncing. Return the bar securely to the rack. This requires a bench that supports a decline position. Record the total barbell weight.
descriptions.it: Sdraiatevi su una panca declinata, il bilanciere deve trovarsi direttamente sopra gli occhi, le ginocchia sono leggermente angolate e i piedi sono ben saldi sul pavimento. Concentratevi, respirate profondamente e afferrate la sbarra a più della larghezza delle spalle. Portatela lentamente verso il basso fino a sfiorare brevemente il petto all'altezza dei capezzoli. Spingere il bilanciere verso l'alto.

descriptions.en: Use a bench that supports a decline position and secure the legs with its supports. Hold a dumbbell at each side of the chest with the wrists over the elbows. Press upward, keeping the shoulder blades supported, then lower under control without forcing the shoulders below a comfortable range. Record the weight of one dumbbell.

Support yourself on parallel dip bars with the arms extended and the shoulders controlled. Bend the elbows and lower the body to a comfortable depth without shrugging or forcing the shoulders backward. Press through the bars to return to the top without swinging. Parallel dip bars are required; this is not a bench dip. For the weighted variant, record only the added weight.
descriptions.it: È un esercizio di forza della parte superiore del corpo. Dip stretti, alla larghezza delle spalle, allenano principalmente i tricipiti, con i principali sinergici che sono il deltoide anteriore, i muscoli pettorali (sternale, clavicolare e minore) e i muscoli romboidali della schiena (in quest'ordine).[1] L'allenamento con le braccia larghe pone ulteriore enfasi sui muscoli pettorali, in modo simile al modo in cui una panca con presa larga si concentrerebbe maggiormente sui pettorali e meno sui tricipiti.

descriptions.en: Sit on a bench with the feet apart and hold one dumbbell. Rest the back of the upper arm against the inner thigh. Curl the weight without moving the upper arm or twisting the torso, then lower under control until the elbow is comfortably extended. Complete the repetitions on each side. Record the weight of the single dumbbell.

Grasp dumbbell with both hands at the sides of the upper plates. Hold dumbbell in front of chest, close to torso. Place feet about shoulderwide apart, keep knees slightly bent.
Squat down until thighs are parallel to floor. Keep back straight, bend and move hips backward to keep knees above feet. Return, keep knees slightly flexed. Repeat.
Keep bodyweight on heels and look ahead or slightly above to keep back straight.

• Setup: Set an adjustable bench to an incline of approximately 45 to 60 degrees.
• Starting Position: Sit back against the bench with a dumbbell in each hand. Let your arms hang straight down toward the floor with your palms facing forward (supinated grip).
• The Curl: Keeping your upper arms stationary and shoulders pinned back against the bench, exhale and curl the weights upward toward your shoulders.
• Peak Contraction: Squeeze your biceps hard at the top of the movement, ensuring your elbows do not swing forward.
• The Descent: Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position, maintaining full control and feeling the stretch in the biceps.

Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand. Step forward with one leg and lower by bending both knees, keeping the front foot planted and the trunk controlled. Push through the front foot to return to the starting stance before changing sides. This is a forward lunge in place, not a walking lunge. Complete the repetitions on each side; record the weight of one dumbbell.

• Starting Position: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hands either on your hips or holding dumbbells at your sides.
• The Stride: Take a wide step forward with your right leg.
• The Descent: Lower your hips until both knees are bent at approximately 90-degree angles.
• The Transition: Drive through your front heel to stand up, bringing your back foot forward to step directly into the next lunge.

Attach a rope to a pulley station set at about chest level.
Step back so you're supporting the weight with arms completely outstretched and assume a staggered (one foot forward) stance. Bend the knees slightly for a stable base.
Retract the scapulae (squeeze your partner's finger with your shoulder blades) and pull the center of the rope slightly up towards the face. A good cue is to think about pulling the ends of the rope apart, not just pulling back.
As you near your face, externally rotate so your knuckles are facing the ceiling.
Hold for one second at the top position and slowly lower.

Set both cable pulleys around chest height and hold one handle in each hand. Step forward into a stable stance with the trunk braced. With a small fixed bend in the elbows, bring the hands together in front of the chest. Return under control without shrugging or changing the elbow angle. Record the load selected on one cable stack and use the same load on both stacks.

Take two dumbbells and lay on a bench, make sure the feet are firmly on the ground and your back is not arched, but has good contact with the bench. The arms are stretched in front of you, about shoulder wide. Bend now the arms a bit and let them down with a half-circle movement to the side. Without changing the angle of the elbow bring them in a fluid movement back up.
descriptions.it: Croci su panca InclinataCroci su panca Inclinata

descriptions.en:
Hold the dumbbells and lay down on a flat bench in such a way that around 1/4 of your head is over the edge. Stretch arms straight up and then lean dumbbells away from your toes to a 10-20 degree angle. Keep upper arm at this angle throughout exercise. Dumbbell shall not be amed at your head, but away over your head. This will maximise gain from exercise with load on triceps all the time.
Pay attention to your elbows and arms: only the triceps are doing the work, the rest of the arms should not move.

Lie on a flat bench and hold an EZ bar above the chest with a comfortable narrow grip. Keep the upper arms mostly still and bend the elbows to lower the bar beside or just behind the forehead within a comfortable range. Extend the elbows to raise it without swinging the shoulders. Record the total weight of the EZ bar.

Set the bar on rack supports at shoulder height. Hold it across the front of the shoulders with the elbows raised and the trunk braced. Unrack it and step back into a stable stance. Bend the knees and hips to squat to a comfortable depth while keeping the elbows lifted and the feet planted. Stand back up without rounding the back, then return the bar securely to the rack.

Lie on your back with the knees bent, feet flat around hip width, and arms relaxed beside the torso. Brace the abdomen gently and press through the whole foot to lift the hips. Stop when the knees, hips, and shoulders form a straight line without arching the lower back. Pause while contracting the glutes, then lower the pelvis under control. Keep the knees tracking over the feet throughout the repetition.

• Start: Hold dumbbells at your sides with palms facing your torso.
• Curl: Lift the weights toward your shoulders while maintaining the neutral grip (like holding a hammer).
• Squeeze: Contract the biceps at the top without moving your elbows forward.
• Lower: Slowly return to the starting position with full control.
descriptions.it: Hummer curl con manubriHummer curl con manubri

descriptions.en: Attach a rope to a low cable. Stand upright and hold the rope ends with the palms facing each other in a neutral grip. Curl by bending the elbows while keeping the upper arms close to the sides. Lower slowly to a comfortable extension without swinging the trunk. Record the selected cable load.

Sit on the floor with the upper back against a stable bench and a padded barbell over the hips. Plant the feet and brace the trunk. Drive through the feet to raise the hips until the torso and thighs align, without arching the lower back. Lower under control while keeping the upper back supported. Record the total barbell weight.

Set an adjustable bench to a moderate incline. Lie back with a dumbbell in each hand above the chest. Keep a small fixed bend in the elbows and open the arms out to the sides within a comfortable range. Bring the weights back above the chest without turning the movement into a press. Record the weight of one dumbbell.
descriptions.it: DistDistensione Panca Inclinata con BilanciereDistensione Panca Inclinata con Bilanciere

descriptions.en:
• Using a neutral grip, lean into an incline bench.
• Take a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip, beginning with the arms straight. This will be your starting position.
• Retract the shoulder blades and flex the elbows to row the dumbbells to your side.
• Pause at the top of the motion, and then return to the starting position.

This exercise works the deltoid muscle of the shoulder. The movement starts with the arms straight, and the hands holding weights at the sides or in front of the body. Body is in a slight forward-leaning position with hips and knees bent a little. Arms are kept straight or slightly bent, and raised through an arc of movement in the coronal plane that terminates when the hands are at approximately shoulder height. Weights are lowered to the starting position, completing one rep. When using a cable machine the individual stands with the coronal plane in line with the pulley, which is at or near the ground.[9] The exercise can be completed one shoulder at a time (with the other hand used to stabilize the body against the weight moved), or with both hands simultaneously if two parallel pulleys are available.
descriptions.it: Alzate LateraliAlzate Laterali

descriptions.en: Adjust the lying leg curl machine so the knees align with its pivot and the lower-leg pad rests above the heels. Lie face down and hold the handles. Bend the knees to bring the pad toward the buttocks without lifting the hips. Lower slowly to a comfortable knee extension. Record the selected machine load.

Adjust the seated leg curl machine so the knees align with its pivot. Place the lower legs over the ankle pad and secure the thigh pad. Keep the back against the support and bend the knees to pull the pad down and backward. Return slowly without lifting the thighs or hips. Record the selected machine load.

The leg extension is a resistance weight training exercise that targets the quadriceps muscle in the legs. The exercise is done using a machine called the Leg Extension Machine. There are various manufacturers of these machines and each one is slightly different. Most gym and weight rooms will have the machine in their facility. The leg extension is an isolated exercise targeting one specific muscle group, the quadriceps. It should not be considered as a total leg workout, such as the squat or deadlift. The exercise consists of bending the leg at the knee and extending the legs, then lowering them back to the original position.
The leg press is a weight training exercise in which the individual pushes a weight or resistance away from them using their legs.

Sit at the low-row station with the feet braced and knees slightly bent. Hold the handle, lengthen the spine, and keep the ribs stacked over the pelvis. Initiate the pull by drawing the shoulder blades back, then bring the handle toward the lower ribs without leaning backward. Pause briefly and return under control until the arms are extended without rounding the lower back.
descriptions.it: Sedersi, appoggiare i piedi sui punti di appoggio e afferrare la sbarra con una presa larga. Tirate il peso con un movimento rapido verso l'ombelico, non in alto. Durante il movimento, tenere le braccia e i gomiti vicini al corpo. Le spalle sono unite. Lasciare scendere lentamente il peso finché le braccia non sono completamente distese.

descriptions.en: Start in a pike position with the hips high, hands slightly wider than shoulder width, and head between the arms. Bend the elbows and lower the crown of the head toward the floor while keeping the hips elevated. Press the floor away until the elbows are straight again. Elevating the feet increases the load, but keep the range controlled and avoid collapsing through the lower back.
descriptions.it:
Posizione di sguardo:
Cane rivolto verso il basso:Il tuo corpo dovrebbe formare una forma a V, con la schiena, le braccia e le gambe dritte. I tuoi fianchi dovrebbero essere in aria.Puoi raggiungere questa posizione camminando con le mani indietro da un plank alto.
Passi:

• Piegare i gomiti di lato, mantenendo la schiena e le gambe dritte e avvicinando la testa al pavimento.
• Raddrizzare le braccia, spingendo i fianchi verso l'alto e mantenendo la schiena e le gambe dritte.
• Ripetere.

descriptions.en: Sit at a preacher bench with the upper arms supported by the angled pad. Hold an EZ bar with the palms facing upward and the wrists comfortable. Curl without lifting the upper arms off the pad, then lower under control to a comfortable elbow extension. This requires a preacher pad, not only a flat bench. Record the total EZ-bar weight.
descriptions.it: Posiziona la barra EZ curl sulle maniglie di riposo davanti alla panca del predicatore. Appoggiati alla panca e afferra la barra EZ curl con i palmi rivolti verso l'alto. Sedersi sulla panca del predicatore in modo che la parte superiore delle braccia poggi sulla parte superiore dell'imbottitura e il petto sia premuto contro l'imbottitura. Abbassa il peso finché i gomiti non sono estesi e le braccia sono dritte. Riporta i pesi al punto di partenza contraendo i bicipiti. Ripetere

descriptions.en: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder width. Brace the trunk and begin by drawing the shoulder blades down, then pull until the chin clears the bar while keeping the chest lifted. Avoid kicking, swinging, or forcing the head forward. Lower under control to straight arms and a stable shoulder position before starting the next repetition.
descriptions.it:
Posizione di partenza:
Iniziare appendendosi alla barra di pull-up, con i palmi rivolti verso l'esterno e i piedi fuori dal pavimento.Le vostre mani dovrebbero essere leggermente più larghe della larghezza delle spalle. Solo leggermente, in modo che i gomiti siano ancora di fronte al corpo piuttosto che esattamente di lato.Il corpo deve essere dritto e puntato leggermente in avanti. Le braccia devono essere distese.
Passi:

• Usa la tua forza per tirare il tuo corpo verso l'alto in modo uniforme, avvicinando il tuo petto alla barra del pull-up e il tuo mento appena sopra di essa. NON sollevarsi usando lo slancio, come i calci.
• Abbassare con attenzione il corpo fino alla posizione di partenza.
• Ripetere.

Suggerimenti:

• Per fare correttamente le trazioni, dovete prima costruire la forza in diverse aree chiave, comprese le spalle, le braccia e gli addominali. Iniziate con le trazioni solo dopo aver acquisito abbastanza forza con altri esercizi.

descriptions.en: Sit on a bench holding a dumbbell in each hand. Hinge the trunk forward and keep the back still. With a small fixed bend in the elbows, raise the arms out to the sides without shrugging or swinging. Lower slowly while maintaining the torso angle. Record the weight of one dumbbell.

Stand holding a pair of dumbbells with the palms facing each other in a neutral grip. Keep the knees slightly bent and hinge at the hips until the torso is inclined forward. Brace the trunk and keep the back still. Pull both dumbbells toward the hips by driving the elbows backward without shrugging, swinging or standing up. Lower under control until the arms are extended, keeping the torso angle constant. No bench is required. Record the weight of one dumbbell; both dumbbells are used together.

• Tighten muscles
• Controlled movement
• Slow movement
• Keep upper body upright
• Do not lean back
• Pull toward chest

This is a variation of the flat bench press designed to emphasize the clavicular head of the pectoralis major (the upper portion). By tilting the torso, the angle of the push changes, shifting more tension to the upper chest and shoulders, which helps achieve a more aesthetic, balanced, and three-dimensional development of the torso.

• 
Bench Adjustment and Preparation: Set the bench to an incline of between 30 and 45 degrees (an incline greater than 45° will place too much strain on the shoulders and reduce the stimulus to the chest). Sit down with a dumbbell on each thigh.

• 
Starting position: Lean back, resting your back against the bench, while using your knees one after the other to push the dumbbells upward to shoulder height.

• 
Anatomical Stabilization: Plant your feet firmly on the floor. Retract your scapulas (bring your shoulder blades together and press them into the bench) to protect your shoulders and stabilize the load.

• 
Eccentric Phase (Lowering): Lower the dumbbells slowly and in a controlled manner toward the upper part of your chest. Your elbows should not splay out to the sides (90°); maintain a safe angle of about 45 to 60 degrees relative to your torso.

• 
Concentric Phase (Lift): Push the dumbbells vertically upward as you exhale. Follow a slightly converging path (without letting them touch at the top). Stop the movement just before locking out your elbows to maintain muscle tension in the upper pectoral.
descriptions.it:
• 
La panca dovrebbe essere inclinata ovunque da 30 a 45 gradi

• 
Assicurati di premere i manubri verso l'alto (perpendicolarmente al pavimento)

descriptions.en: Set a bench to a moderate incline inside a rack and position the bar above the upper chest. Set the rack supports and safeties before starting. Lie back with the feet planted and shoulder blades supported. Unrack the bar, lower it under control toward the upper chest, then press upward without lifting the hips or bouncing the bar. Return the bar securely to the rack after the set.
descriptions.it: Distensione Panca Inclinata con BilanciereDistensione Panca Inclinata con Bilanciere

descriptions.en: Adjust the shoulder-press machine seat so the handles start around shoulder height. Sit with the back supported and feet planted. Hold the handles, keep the ribs down, and press upward in a controlled movement without shrugging or arching the back. Lower to the starting position under control. Select the weight on the machine and keep the movement within a comfortable range.

Set a bench with an upright back support inside a rack. Sit with the feet planted and hold the bar at upper-chest height, slightly wider than shoulder width. Press overhead without arching the back, then lower under control. Return the bar securely to the rack. Record the total barbell weight.

Sit on a bench with an almost upright back support and the feet planted. Hold a dumbbell at each shoulder with the wrists above the elbows. Press overhead without pushing with the legs or arching the lower back. Lower under control to shoulder height. This is the seated variant and requires a bench. Record the weight of one dumbbell.

Sit in a seated calf raise machine with the balls of the feet on the platform and the thigh pads secured above the knees. Release the machine support, raise the heels, then lower slowly within a comfortable ankle range. Keep the knees bent and avoid bouncing. Re-engage the support after the set. Record the selected machine load.

Use a standing calf raise machine with the shoulder pads adjusted and the balls of the feet on its platform. Keep the knees nearly straight and the trunk still. Raise the heels without bouncing, pause briefly, then lower under control within a comfortable range. Record the selected machine load.
descriptions.it: Salite sulla macchina per i sollevamenti dei polpacci, dovreste essere in grado di spingere completamente i polpacci verso il basso. State dritti, non inarcate la schiena e non piegate le gambe. Tiratevi su il più possibile. Fate una piccola pausa di 1-2 secondi e scendete lentamente.

descriptions.en: Stand over a barbell with a wide stance and the toes turned outward comfortably. Bend the hips and knees and grip the bar inside the legs. Brace the trunk and push through the floor to stand, keeping the bar close. Finish upright without leaning backward. Lower by bending the hips and knees under control. Record the total barbell weight.

• Start with a dumbbell in each hand and your palms facing your torso. Keep your back straight with a slight bend in the knees and bend forward at the waist. Your torso should be almost parallel to the floor. Make sure to keep your head up. Your upper arms should be close to your torso and parallel to the floor. Your forearms should be pointed towards the floor as you hold the weights. There should be a 90-degree angle formed between your forearm and upper arm. This is your starting position.
• Now, while keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and use your triceps to lift the weights until the arm is fully extended. Focus on moving the forearm.
• After a brief pause at the top contraction, inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
• Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

Variations: This exercise can be executed also one arm at a time much like the one arm rows are performed.
Also, if you like the one arm variety, you can use a low pulley handle instead of a dumbbell for better peak contraction. In this case, the palms should be facing up (supinated grip) as opposed to the torso (neutral grip).

Grab the cable, stand with your feet shoulder wide, keep your back straight and lean forward a little. Push the bar down, making sure the elbows don't move during the exercise. Rotate your hands outwards at the very end and go back to the initial position without pause.

Stand on one foot and use a wall lightly for balance. Keep the supporting knee nearly straight, raise the heel, then lower slowly to the floor without bouncing. Keep the pelvis level. Complete the prescribed repetitions on each side. No external weight or machine is required.
descriptions.it:
• Stare in piedi sul pavimento o sul bordo di un gradino per aumentare il raggio di movimento. Sollevare un piede, appoggiando la parte superiore sul polpaccio.
• Sollevare i talloni fino a stare in piedi sulle punte dei piedi.
• Resta in questa posizione per tre secondi, poi abbassa il piede senza toccare il suolo con il tallone.

descriptions.en: Sit at a high-cable pulldown station and secure the thighs under the pads. Hold the bar with an overhand grip comfortably wider than shoulder width. Pull toward the upper chest by driving the elbows down, without swinging or pulling behind the neck. Return under control until the arms are extended. Record the selected cable load.

Set both cable pulleys around shoulder height and hold the opposite handles with the arms in front of you. Keep a small fixed bend in the elbows and open the arms out to the sides without shrugging or arching the lower back. Return under control. Record the load selected on one cable stack and use the same load on both stacks.

Set an adjustable bench to a moderate incline and lie face down with the chest supported. Hold a dumbbell in each hand below the shoulders. With a small fixed bend in the elbows, raise the arms out to the sides without shrugging or lifting the chest. Lower slowly. Record the weight of one dumbbell.
descriptions.it: Le alzate posteriori sono un esercizio complementare e di isolamento per il deltoide posteriore. Essendo focalizzato su un muscolo specifico, solitamente, si usano pesi leggeri ripetizioni fra le 10 e le 15 per serie.

descriptions.en: Hang from a pull-up bar with the shoulders controlled. Bend the knees and raise them toward the chest, finishing with a small controlled curl of the pelvis. Lower slowly without swinging, kicking or arching the lower back. Work within a range that allows the trunk to remain controlled. No added weight is required.
descriptions.it: sollevamento gambe 90° alla sbarra è un esercizio molto intenso che coinvolge tutta la muscolatura addominale.

descriptions.en:
Starting position:
Stand with back straight.
Steps:

• Take a large step forward with your left leg.
• Bring your pelvis down until you almost touch the floor with your right knee.
• Bring your pelvis back up.
• Return to the starting position by stepping back.
• Repeat, switching legs each time.
descriptions.it:
• Stai in piedi a schiena dritta
• Fai un grande passo avanti con la gamba sinistra
• Abbassa il bacino fino a toccare quasi il pavimento con il ginocchio destro
• Tendi il bacino in avanti
• Ritorna in posizione eretta facendo un passo indietro
• Ripeti, alternando le gambe ogni volta

descriptions.en:
Starting position:
Stand hip-width apart, with your kettlebell centered between your ankles. Your back should be straight, your head facing forward.
Steps:

• Hinge at the hips and slightly bend at the knees to put your hands on the kettlebell handles. Your back should be straight as you perform the movement.
• Grab the kettlebell handles, with your hands pushing in opposite directions as if to pull the handle apart.
• While contacting your abs and glutes, stand straight up.
• Hinge at the hips again to bring the kettlebell back down, similarly to step 1.
• Repeat from step 3.

Tips:

• Be sure you're performing the movements correctly, as doing otherwise can lead to injury. For example, do not squat instead of hinging at the hips, do not round your back while reaching for the kettlebell, and do not lean back while standing up.
descriptions.it:
Posizione di partenza:
Stare alla larghezza delle anche, con il kettlebell centrato tra le caviglie. La schiena deve essere dritta, la testa rivolta in avanti.
Passi:

• Inclinarsi sui fianchi e piegare leggermente le ginocchia per mettere le mani sulle maniglie del kettlebell. La schiena deve essere dritta mentre si esegue il movimento.
• Afferrare le maniglie del kettlebell, con le mani che spingono in direzioni opposte come se si volesse separare la maniglia.
• Mentre contattate gli addominali e i glutei, alzatevi in piedi.
• Inclinarsi di nuovo sui fianchi per riportare il kettlebell verso il basso, in modo simile al passo 1.
• Ripetere dal punto 3.

Suggerimenti:

• Assicuratevi di eseguire i movimenti correttamente, perché altrimenti potreste farvi male. Per esempio, non accovacciarsi invece di piegarsi sui fianchi, non arrotondare la schiena mentre si raggiunge il kettlebell, e non piegarsi all'indietro mentre ci si alza.

descriptions.en: Grab your dumbbells and lay flat on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the ground (use a bench if you have one). Press the weights up, locking out your elbows (A). Lower them slowly until your upper arms are resting on the floor (B) close to your body. Pause here before explosively pressing back up. Squeeze your chest hard and repeat.

Drop into a strong plank position, bringing your hands close together until they're almost touching. (picture 1)Bend your elbows to slowly bring your chest to the floor (picture 2). Keep your elbows close to your body as you push back up explosively. Repeat. Ensure you take your time lowering on each rep, keeping your form sharp.

Place the hands on a stable bench and walk the feet back until the body forms a straight line. Bend the elbows to lower the chest toward the bench, then press back up while keeping the trunk braced. Keep the bench fixed and avoid letting the hips sag. The hands are elevated; the feet stay on the floor.

descriptions.en:
Decline push-ups are another modified version of the traditional push-up that target the upper body muscles in a different way. To perform a decline push-up, elevate your feet on an elevated surface, such as a bench, chair, or step, while placing your hands on the ground in a push-up position. Lower your body towards the ground while maintaining a straight line from your shoulders to your ankles, and then push back up to the starting position.
Unlike the inclined push-up, the decline push-up places more emphasis on the shoulders and triceps, while still engaging the chest muscles to a lesser extent. By elevating your feet, you increase the difficulty of the exercise by placing more weight on your upper body, forcing your shoulders and triceps to work harder to push your body back up. The decline push-up can be a great way to challenge your upper body strength and improve your ability to perform other push-up variations. As with any exercise, be sure to use proper form and start with a height that is appropriate for your strength and fitness level.

Downward movement
•  Pull the bar down so that it passes close to your chin and touches the upper part of your chest.
•  Keep the rest of your body still.

The lat pulldown is an important exercise for strengthening the back and improving posture, which can contribute to a healthier life. To perform this exercise correctly and avoid injury, it is important to follow a few key steps:

• 
Position yourself in front of the cable machine with your knees slightly bent and your feet on the floor.

• 
Grip the cable handle with your palms facing each other and your hands shoulder-width apart.

• 
Pull the handle down until it touches or comes close to your chest, holding the position for one or two seconds.

• 
Slowly raise the handle back to the starting position, making sure to keep your arms and hands straight and your back straight throughout the movement.

Stand with the feet around hip width and use a wall lightly for balance if needed. Keep the knees nearly straight and raise both heels to stand on the balls of the feet. Pause briefly, then lower slowly to the floor without bouncing. This bodyweight version requires no calf machine or external weight.

Set both cable pulleys around head height and hold the opposite handles in a crossed setup. Keep the upper arms mostly still and extend the elbows down and outward in a comfortable cross-body path. Return under control without shrugging or swinging the torso. Record the selected load on one cable stack; both stacks are used together.

Stand with the feet around shoulder width and keep the whole foot on the floor. Brace the trunk, bend the knees and hips together, and lower into a squat to a comfortable depth while keeping the knees aligned with the feet. Stand back up by pushing through the feet. Use a controlled movement without bouncing; no bench, box or external weight is required.

• Keep the elbows fixed
• Engage the muscles
• Don't use momentum
• Controlled movement
• Slow movement
• Don't overextend

Stand in a split stance holding a dumbbell in each hand, with both feet on the floor. Bend both knees to lower the body vertically, keeping the front foot planted and the trunk controlled. Push through the front foot to rise without stepping. Complete the repetitions on each side. No bench is required. Record the weight of one dumbbell.

The single arm cable lateral raise is a variation of the lateral raise and an exercise used to build the muscles of the shoulders.

• Position a cable at the lowest position possible and attach a single handle.
• Reach across your body and grab the handle with a neutral grip.
• Keep the elbow slightly bent and pull the handle across your body and raise laterally.
• Slowly lower the handle back to the starting position under control.

Use a hack squat machine with the back and shoulders supported by its pads. Plant the feet securely on the platform and release the supports. Bend the hips and knees to lower within a comfortable range while keeping the back supported. Push through the feet to rise without bouncing, then re-engage the supports. Record the machine load.

The biceps curl machine is designed to isolate the biceps muscles and provide a controlled range of motion. Sit on the machine with your back against the pad and adjust the seat so your arms are aligned with the machine's handles or pads. Grip the handles firmly, keeping your elbows fixed in place, and curl the handles upward by contracting your biceps. Slowly lower the handles to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement.

Stand holding a pair of dumbbells with an underhand grip, palms facing forward. Keep the knees slightly bent and hinge at the hips until the torso is inclined forward. Brace the trunk and keep the back still. Pull the dumbbells toward the hips with the elbows close to the torso, maintaining the underhand grip. Lower under control until the arms are extended without swinging or standing up. No bench is required. Record the weight of one dumbbell; both dumbbells are used together.

Set a cable pulley low and hold one handle with the arm slightly behind the torso. Face away from the stack in a stable stance. Curl by bending the elbow while keeping the upper arm still and the shoulder in a comfortable position. Lower under control without swinging. Complete the repetitions on each side. Record the selected cable load.

Attach a rope to a cable pulley and face away from the stack. Hold the rope above and behind the head, with the elbows pointing upward. Brace the trunk in a stable stance and extend the elbows without moving the upper arms or arching the back. Bend the elbows to return under control. Record the selected cable load.

The push-up is a fundamental bodyweight exercise that targets the chest, arms, and shoulders while engaging the core for stability. It requires no equipment and is excellent for building upper body strength.
Instructions:

• Start in a plank position with hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width, feet together, and body in a straight line from head to heels.
• Engage your core and lower your body by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body or flared slightly outward.
• Lower until your chest nearly touches the ground while maintaining a neutral spine.
• Push through your palms to return to the starting position, fully extending your arms.

• Starting Position: Kneel on the floor with the ab wheel in front of you.
• Grip the Wheel: Hold the handles firmly.
• Roll Out: Slowly roll the wheel forward, extending your body while keeping your core tight.
• Return: Pull the wheel back towards your knees, maintaining tension in your core.

Sit on a bench with the feet flat and the knees bent. Place one dumbbell across the thighs just above the knees and hold it securely. Raise both heels, pause briefly, then lower slowly without bouncing. Keep the weight balanced and the torso still. Record the weight of the single dumbbell.

This exercise involves holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height and performing a squat. It targets the lower body muscles, including the quads, hamstrings, and glutes, while also engaging the core and upper body.

Sit on the floor with the upper back against a stable bench. Place one dumbbell across the hips and hold it securely. Plant the feet and raise the hips until the thighs and torso align without arching the lower back. Lower under control while keeping the upper back supported. Record the weight of the single dumbbell.

The Weighted Crunch is a variation of the classic crunch exercise that involves adding resistance (a weight) to increase the intensity of the abdominal work.

• Lay down
• (Optional) Bend your knees to add difficulty
• (Optional) Bend your knees and let your feet rest on a bench or a box or something (90 degree angle on knees)
• Lift your head and torso while bending your back forward (if you don't it's a sit-up and also involves some back muscles). The higher you go, the more you should feel your abs contracting.
• Go back to starting position an repeat
This exercise involves holding a dumbbell in each hand and stepping back into a lunge position, then returning to standing. It primarily targets the glutes, hamstrings, and quadriceps.

This exercise involves holding a dumbbell in each hand and bending forward at the hips while keeping the back straight, then returning to a standing position. It primarily targets the hamstrings and glutes.

The machine lateral raise is an isolation exercise that targets the medial (side) deltoid muscle to build wider, more defined shoulders. The machine's fixed path of motion provides greater stability than dumbbells, making it ideal for beginners or those who want to focus solely on muscle activation.

Use a pull-up bar with parallel handles and hold them with the palms facing each other. Begin with the arms extended and the shoulders controlled. Pull upward by driving the elbows down without kicking or swinging. Lower slowly to the starting position. Parallel handles are required for this neutral grip. For the weighted variant, record only the added weight.

Stand holding the barbell in front of the thighs with the knees slightly bent. Brace the trunk and push the hips backward, keeping the bar close to the legs and the back still. Lower only as far as the hip hinge allows without rounding the back. Drive the hips forward to stand tall without leaning backward. Keep the knee angle nearly constant and lower each repetition under control; the bar need not reach the floor.

The Bulgarian split squat consists of performing a squat on one leg with the rear foot resting on a raised platform. Elevating your back leg on a bench creates instability and increases the range of motion of the exercise.

Keep arms straight but not locked, pulling with your lats, not your shoulders.
Don’t let your shoulders shrug up during the movement.

Stand holding one dumbbell in one hand. Shift onto one leg with the knee slightly bent. Hinge at the hips while extending the free leg backward, keeping the pelvis level and the back still. Lower only as far as you can control, then drive the hip forward to stand. Complete the repetitions on each side. Record the single dumbbell weight.

Lie on the back with one foot planted and the knee bent. Lift the other foot off the floor. Brace the trunk and push through the planted foot to raise the hips without rotating the pelvis or arching the lower back. Lower slowly and complete the repetitions on each side. No external weight is required.

• Lay down
• Place your hands near your butt (often slightly in front or under or both)
• Raise your legs, but about 70% of the way you should be able to also raise your pelvis
• (optional/variable) Hold 1/2 seconds at the top
• Go back to starting position

• The barbell full squat is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups in the lower body, including the quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes.
• Proper form is crucial for maximizing results and preventing injuries during the barbell full squat. This includes maintaining a shoulder-width stance, creating whole body tension, controlling your descent, and maintaining proper depth and knee positioning.
• Assistance moves such as the front squat, goblet squat, split squat, and Bulgarian split squat can help improve your performance in the barbell full squat by targeting specific muscle groups and improving overall technique.
• To achieve new personal records in your back squat, gradually increase weight over time, vary rep ranges and sets to stimulate muscle growth, and prioritize rest and recovery between training sessions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell on your upper back.
Step 2: Keep your back straight, chest up, and core engaged.
Step 3: Take a step back with one leg and lower your body by bending both knees. Ensure that your back knee nearly touches the ground.
Step 4: Push off your back foot to return to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat the movement with the other leg.
Continue alternating between legs for the desired repetitions.

• Sit upright in a hammerstrength decline chest press machine while squeezing your shoulder blades together and placing your heels firmly on the ground underneath your knees.
• The back pad should be contact with your head, shoulders, and butt at all times.
• Grab ahold of the handles with an overhand grip just outside shoulder-width apart just below your chest.
• Keeping your core braced by breathing into your stomach and flexing the abdominal muscles, push through your palms to extend your elbows while keeping them at a 45 degree angle from your torso.
• Once your arms are fully extended, return to the starting position.

Set a barbell on rack supports at upper-chest height. Stand with the feet around hip width, hold the bar slightly wider than shoulder width, and unrack it. Brace the trunk and press overhead without bending the knees or driving with the legs. Lower under control to the upper chest and return the bar to the rack. Record the total barbell weight.

Stand with the feet planted and hold one dumbbell at shoulder height. Brace the trunk and press overhead without leaning sideways, arching the back or pushing with the legs. Lower under control to shoulder height. Complete the repetitions on each side. No bench is required. Record the weight of the single dumbbell.

Stand holding a dumbbell at each shoulder, with the feet planted and the trunk braced. Press both dumbbells overhead without bending the knees, pushing with the legs or arching the lower back. Lower under control to shoulder height. Keep the wrists above the elbows and work within a comfortable range. No bench is required. Record the weight of one dumbbell.
